name: Your Berlin Street in 1928
place: Your own address · c. 1928 and today
alt: Example personalised aerial print: a Berlin square in 1928 and today
storyHtml:
Type your address and see your street from above in 1928, the way a survey plane photographed it, with the same spot today below it. Most Berlin Altbau blocks were already standing, so you can often find your own courtyard. If your house is newer, you see what stood there before it.

The print carries your street, district, map coordinates and an optional line of your own.
storyHtmlDigital: The digital version of my print: your own Berlin spot in the 1928 aerial photograph, with the same spot today below it, at the same scale, and your title, area line and coordinates.

visualCreditsHtml:
Image credits and AI process

I selected this close upward view of the Siegessäule and directed the architectural corrections while keeping its angle and gouache style. The artwork was generated and edited with OpenAI ImageGen, then enhanced with Adobe Firefly Upscaler. It is an artistic interpretation, not a measured architectural drawing.

Photographic inputs used in the artistic adaptation:

BugWarp — "Berlin Victory Column - BugWarp 01.jpg" (12 August 2024), CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication; overall column and gallery reference.
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Berlin_Victory_Column_-_BugWarp_01.jpg
https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/

Gerd Eichmann — "Berlin-Siegessaeule-24-Engel-2022-gje.jpg" (20 April 2022), Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0); statue-detail input inherited by the selected image and later revisions. This inherited use is treated as an adaptation for attribution purposes.
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Berlin-Siegessaeule-24-Engel-2022-gje.jpg
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

Changes include a new illustrated viewpoint, colour, lighting and gouache-like texture, correction of the top drum, AI detail enhancement and a uniform horizontal crop for the 50 x 70 cm version. The 30 x 40 cm composition is retained. These are actual generator references; the source photographs are not the item being sold. Neither photographer endorses this artwork. Source licences and their permitted rights remain in effect; the CC BY source is supplied without warranties under its licence.
cardSummary: Berlin’s Siegessäule rises above the colonnade in this close, upward view. Cobalt blue, warm stone and gold give the Victory Column a strong contrast.

visualCreditsHtml:
Kottbusser Tor: source photographs and changes

Gunnar Klack — Wohnbebauung-Kottbusser-Tor-Nordbloecke-Neues-Kreuzberger-Zentrum-03-2017a.jpg, 25 March 2017, own work on Wikimedia Commons; CC BY-SA 4.0. This photograph was an architectural input for the shallow NKZ curve and facade rhythm.

Gunnar Klack — Neues-Kreuzberger-Zentrum-Kottbusser-Tor-Skalitzer-Str-Berlin-Kreuzberg-08-2017a.jpg, 5 August 2017, own work on Wikimedia Commons; CC BY-SA 4.0. This photograph was an architectural input for the broad recesses, white solid bays and yellow paired windows.

Changes to the photographic references: the scene, viewpoint, surface texture, lighting and colours were artistically reinterpreted with OpenAI ImageGen, and the facade was then revised using both photographs. Adobe Firefly Upscaler enlarged the resulting 1086 × 1448 pixel artwork to 4344 × 5792 pixels, synthetically enhancing fine detail. For the 50 × 70 cm version, a uniform 3:4 to 5:7 crop removed 4.762% of the original width from the two sides combined, retaining the full image height without stretching. The 30 × 40 cm composition is unchanged. This is an artistic interpretation, not a measured drawing or a current-state documentary photograph; synthetic enhancement is not native captured detail or a physical print proof.

For distribution, the artwork is treated as an adaptation of those CC BY-SA 4.0 photographs. Any copyrightable contributions in the adaptation are offered under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International. Retain Gunnar Klack's name, both source links, the licence link and this complete change history. Adaptations must use the same or a compatible licence; no additional legal or technical restriction is imposed on the rights granted by that licence. The photographer does not endorse this artwork.

The licensed copyright material is supplied without warranties under CC BY-SA 4.0, section 5. This notice does not limit mandatory consumer rights for the purchased product. The licence covers only rights its licensors can grant; it does not grant trademark, personality or privacy rights, or independent rights in separately protected works depicted. Room mockups and the 3D styling video are separate visualisations and are outside this artwork licence.

visualCreditsHtml:
Mehringplatz

Source-bound artistic reconstruction using Geoportal Berlin ALKIS building footprints, 2026 orthophotography and public-tree data. Official data: Datenlizenz Deutschland - Zero - Version 2.0.
https://gdi.berlin.de/services/wfs/alkis?service=WFS&request=GetCapabilities
https://gdi.berlin.de/geonetwork/srv/api/records/6067c376-47e9-49d7-8d17-d3e56c0b8dd0
https://gdi.berlin.de/services/wfs/baumbestand?service=WFS&request=GetCapabilities
https://www.govdata.de/dl-de/zero-2-0

Buildings follow source footprints; paths, lawns, tree crowns and the monument are simplified art. This is not a cadastral or measured construction drawing. Space Grotesk by Florian Karsten, SIL OFL 1.1; lettering is outlined. No reference photographs are included in the download.

Walk of Berlin | walkofberlin.com

50 x 70 cm adaptation: uniform 3:4 to 5:7 crop, full image height retained; 4.762% of the original width removed from the two sides combined. No stretching. The 30 x 40 cm composition is unchanged.

visualCreditsHtml:
Steinstücken historical geography artwork.

Boundary data provenance: Geoportal Berlin / Senatsverwaltung für Stadtentwicklung, Bauen und Wohnen Berlin, ALKIS Berlin Ortsteile together with Verlauf der Berliner Mauer, 1989. The red political boundary is derived from those official data; it is not the Wall's front-wall line. The official data use Datenlizenz Deutschland – Zero – Version 2.0.
ALKIS Ortsteile: https://gdi.berlin.de/services/wfs/alkis_ortsteile?service=WFS&request=GetCapabilities
Wall/boundary data: https://gdi.berlin.de/services/wfs/berlinermauer?service=WFS&request=GetCapabilities
Aerial-photo metadata: https://gdi.berlin.de/services/wfs/luftbild_1989_10?service=WFS&request=GetCapabilities
Licence: https://www.govdata.de/dl-de/zero-2-0

Upstream corridor selection used Bernhard-Beyer-Straße road geometry from © OpenStreetMap contributors, 15 October 2026 snapshot. That road located a clipping band within the official West Berlin polygon. The final illustration uses the resulting corridor polygon to limit the local composition and to calculate a schematic road axis; the final red line follows the official political boundary. No OpenStreetMap tiles or source map images are included.

The ODbL notice applies to the source database. This acknowledgement does not assign that database licence to the entire poster or claim that the final red boundary was traced from an OpenStreetMap map image.
